grade: C provisional - playable core and JSON round-trip, but restart and pointer controls remain broken
strengths: The real editor draws and erases bricks; normal keyboard launch moves the ball and arrow keys move the paddle.
Controlled collision/life fixtures confirm brick removal, score updates and three misses reaching game over.

Actual downloaded JSON bytes round-trip through the real file-input handler. Pi repaired initially stationary ball launch and a missing FileReader.readAsText call. Its final 34 authored tests pass in the protected unpiped run.
defects: The Get ready overlay remains visible after launch. Source launchBall() does not hide it, obscuring the playing field and intercepting pointer interaction.
Mouse movement always returns early because the handler requires classList.contains(''), which is false. Keyboard movement works.
Restart reuses the surviving mutable brick array instead of restoring the edited layout. The independent fixture starts with two bricks, destroys one, then restarts with only the survivor.
Restart directly calls loop() while an existing requestAnimationFrame chain remains live, producing two pending animation loops and potentially accelerating simulation.
The shared 60-minute deadline ended the attempt. A proof start/end pair and passing tests did not yield completion of the requested workflow.
